newsitem.title: USA: Motorola limits Sportstrax promotion - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Motorola limits Sportstrax promotion - NYT.

text.p: Just months after it won a legal battle to give it the right to broadcast up-to-the-second basketball scores over its pager network, Motorola Inc has stopped actively promoting the product, the New York Times said.

In Monday's edition, the Times said that the product, Sportstrax can still be purchased, but that Motorola has been more intent on promoting a rival pager, which gives National Basketball Association scores with at least five minutes' delay.
In January, Motorola won a court ruling that NBA scores are news, not proprietary information.
But since then, it has developed an alliance with ESPN, the cable television network owned by Walt Disney Co, called "ESPN to Go."
"We are simply voluntarily abiding by the NBA's guidelines," which stipulates that scores should be broadcast no more than four times per quarter, said Eric Handler, a spokesman for ESPN.
